CurrentPrincipal.description:
The caller, as this organization sees them.

`roles` is here so a client can render navigation that matches what the caller may do. It is
guidance for the interface and nothing more: the backend re-decides every request, so a client
that ignored this and showed every button would be refused rather than obeyed (contract §14).
CurrentPrincipal.title: CurrentPrincipal

DependencyResource.description:
Endpoints as type and id only.

Deliberately no titles. A dependency tells you your work is waiting on `work:5f3a`; what
`work:5f3a` says is a separate question with its own visibility answer (BR-W-18), and folding it
in here would route around that.
DependencyResource.title: DependencyResource

get.description:
Who the caller is, in this organization.

The token says which human is calling; it deliberately never says which organization or what
they may do there (security-model §2). This is where those two questions are answered, and it is
what lets a client render navigation that matches the caller's roles instead of rendering
everything and discovering the refusals one request at a time.

put.description:
One call, one transaction, whether or not the seat is currently occupied.

`PUT` because the request states the desired end state rather than an operation: this person is
the owner. Which matrix cell that needs — `ASSIGN` for unowned Work, `REASSIGN` when somebody is
being displaced — depends on the current state, and the service decides it. A router that chose
would be a router implementing authorization policy (contract §3).

No `If-Match`: the precondition here is about who owns the Work, which the service reads and
acts on inside one transaction, not about a version the caller read earlier.
